YOUR EVERYDAY GUIDE

How to use HappyLulu

From installation to a daily routine, optional connections and safe updates. Follow the steps here without leaving the site.

Mac 1.5.18 build34 · Windows 1.5.13

1. Install or replace the app2. First launch3. Check your day4. Edit today’s arrival5. Workday modes and days off6. Connect optional plugins7. Choose a theme and icon8. View and preserve records9. Update to a new version10. Troubleshooting11. Mac and Windows differences

1. Install or replace the app

Mac 1.5.18 · build34

  1. Get the Mac DMG or ZIP from Downloads. It requires macOS 13 or later. The Universal app includes Apple silicon and Intel binaries.
  2. Quit the running HappyLulu before replacing it. Open the DMG and move the app to Applications or ~/Applications. For a ZIP, extract it and move the app to that location.
  3. Replace the app in the same location, then launch it. Your records and settings are outside the app; do not remove their folders to reinstall.

Windows 1.5.13

  1. The site's Windows download is the smaller runtime-required.zip. Use Windows 10/11 x64 and install .NET 10 Desktop Runtime x64. Choose Desktop Runtime rather than the SDK or the general .NET Runtime.
  2. Extract the entire ZIP into a folder you will keep. Run HappyLulu.exe from the extracted folder, not inside the ZIP.
  3. For an update, right-click the tray icon and quit, then replace the app files in that folder. If you move the folder after enabling startup, set startup again.

The official Windows release also provides a larger ZIP with the runtime included. This self-contained ZIP needs no separate .NET installation. Read Windows release details to choose a package. See Mac 1.5.18 release details for the current Mac changes.

Apple Developer ID signing and notarization, and Windows publisher signing, are not complete. If your operating system blocks launch, verify the download source and your organization's installation policy. Do not disable security protections globally.

2. First launch

  1. Find HappyLulu in the Mac menu bar or Windows notification area. On Windows, also check the hidden-icons list.
  2. Click the Mac menu bar icon or departure time, or left-click the Windows tray icon, to open today. Use the Mac panel's settings button, or right-click the Windows tray icon → Settings, for preferences.
  3. In General, select Korean or English and a remaining-time unit. In Work, set your work and break durations. The defaults are 8 hours of work plus a 1-hour break.
  4. If you already arrived before launching the app, enter today's arrival manually. The app does not infer attendance while it was closed.

Mac attempts login-item registration on first launch; macOS may require approval. A startup preference you turned off stays off. On Windows, enable Start when signing in to Windows yourself in Settings → General.

Basic attendance needs no account or calendar permission. Enable optional plugins later if you need them.

3. Check your day

On Mac, Settings → General → Show expected departure in menu bar is on by default. When on, it shows Leave 18:00 · 91 min left; when off, it shows only 91 min left. Changes apply immediately and the choice survives restart.

At or after expected departure, leaving this option on shows only the expected departure time. Turning it off shows Ready to leave. Waiting for arrival, Day off today and Leave day labels stay unchanged.

  1. Make sure the app is running before arrival. Mac records the first valid observation when launched as a login item or when the screen is actually unlocked. Windows records an actual session-unlock event while running.
  2. Open today to check arrival, workday mode and expected departure. Later unlocks do not overwrite an existing arrival.
  3. Correct a wrong arrival manually and select a half-day when needed. The Mac panel also shows up to three connected events for today; open Calendar in Settings for the full view.

Automatic detection begins at 06:00 local time. For regular work or afternoon off, an observation from 06:00 through 07:59:59 is recorded as 08:00 on the same day. A 06:30 observation gives an 08:00 arrival and 17:00 departure with default hours. Before 06:00 is excluded; morning off retains its 13:00–15:00 window.

Manually launching the app, waking from sleep or activating a session alone does not create a past arrival. Unlocking at home first can record that time. The app does not check your office location or Wi-Fi.

Select milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or hours/minutes for remaining time. Hours round up to one decimal place. From 30 minutes after expected departure, the app shows extra elapsed minutes; after two hours, it shows the meal-time reference. These do not determine approved work or payment.

Automatic attendance · Departure calculation and display · Extra time and meal reference

4. Edit today’s arrival

Mac: click the four digits

  1. Click the arrival time in the menu bar panel. Without a record, the editor suggests the current time.
  2. Type the four HH:mm digits or use the + above and − below each digit. Digits do not carry or wrap.
  3. Press Enter, click elsewhere or close the panel to save. Escape cancels. With no arrival, closing an unchanged suggested time also saves it if valid.

You can also edit today's arrival in Settings → Work. Changing only the time keeps the current manual workday selection or automatic calendar decision.

Windows: use the manual-entry dialog

Left-click the tray icon → Enter manually, choose today's time and regular work, morning off or afternoon off, then save. Windows does not have the Mac digit-by-digit editor or panel autosave.

Regular work and afternoon off accept 08:00–10:00; morning off accepts 13:00–15:00. The final minute is included. The time must be today and cannot be in the future. Manual 06:30 input is not normalized to 08:00. At 09:20, 09:00 is valid and 09:30 is not.

Invalid input keeps the existing record and shows an error. See arrival editing details for the save rules.

5. Workday modes and days off

On Mac, click the selected mode in the panel or open Settings → Work → Today’s work / leave. Choose one of five modes without connecting a calendar.

  • Regular work: work plus break duration. An explicit selection applies zero early-leave minutes, including on the last Friday.
  • Morning off: arrive 13:00–15:00 and leave four hours after arrival.
  • Afternoon off: arrive 08:00–10:00 and leave four hours after arrival. Half-days add no break or Friday reduction.
  • Lulu Day: reduce regular work by 120 minutes. It does not combine with a half-day.
  • Annual / official leave: pause today's automatic arrival and countdown while preserving an existing arrival. See the retained time in the date's history details.

A selection applies only today and does not create an arrival. A mode change is rejected if the existing time is outside that mode's allowed window. Manual choices take priority over automatic half-day recognition. Select regular work or a half-day, or save a valid arrival, to resume from annual / official leave.

Without a manual override, regular work ends two hours earlier on the last Friday of each month. There is no holiday substitution or carryover. Windows 1.5.13 supports regular work, morning off and afternoon off. It does not include Lulu Day, annual / official leave or the explicit regular-work override that removes Friday's reduction.

Day off today clears today's arrival after confirmation and pauses automatic recording. It differs from annual / official leave. On Mac, choose annual / official leave when you want to retain the time. Enter a valid arrival manually to resume after a day off.

These controls do not submit company leave requests or calculate leave balances. Workday mode details · Automatic half-day recognition

6. Connect optional plugins

In Mac Settings → Plugin management, install and enable Calendar, DaouOffice or Leave recognition. These three modules are bundled with the app; this is not a marketplace for external downloads. Installed modules appear below the sidebar divider.

DaouOffice is developed by 손정열 (Son Jeongyeol); Calendar and Leave recognition by HappyLulu contributors. Turning a module off stops its work while preserving saved connections and attendance. Re-enabling it restores saved routing; an explicit “Not connected” choice remains respected.

Calendar: accounts, access and selection before reading

  1. Enable Calendar and open its settings. Choose Open Internet Accounts and add your Google or company CalDAV account to macOS. macOS manages these credentials.
  2. Click Allow calendar access and grant full calendar access. The first event lookup also needs read access; add-events-only permission cannot support viewing or bidirectional sync. Opening the window alone does not request permission.
  3. Choose the feature source for events and half-day recognition. Select the calendars to display in the DaouOffice calendar and Google calendar selectors. Empty selections show no events.
  4. Open the event view and choose Refresh events to read the selected calendars. Stop here if you only want to view events. Granting access, selecting calendars and refreshing do not start bidirectional event writes.
  5. For optional bidirectional sync, select one test calendar from each of two different accounts and complete the account and connection confirmations. Open the first sync preview and review additions, deferred items and conflicts.
  6. Only explicitly clicking Start bidirectional sync starts writing events. Reading or previewing alone does not start sync.

Recurring events are copied as individual occurrences from 30 days ago through 365 days ahead. Invitations become personal copies without reinviting attendees; the original invitation is protected. Deletions are not propagated automatically. Choose a side for conflicts and review a fresh preview after pausing. Check both web calendars after local saves: server round-trip verification remains pending for this beta.

DaouOffice: read company events and leave

  1. Enable the DaouOffice connection in its plugin settings. Enter your company's base HTTPS address, your own login ID and password.
  2. Choose Save and fetch. The password is kept in the Mac Keychain. Results include this year's leave, remaining/used leave and your calendar events for this month.
  3. If a CAPTCHA appears, a person must read the image, enter it and choose Confirm and fetch. Request a new image or cancel when needed. Automatic fetching pauses while awaiting your answer.
  4. Select the source separately for calendar events, leave status and half-day recognition. Normal fetching refreshes every 15 minutes while the app runs; failures retain the last successful results.

DaouOffice is read-only: it does not submit leave, create, modify or delete events. Mac calendar bidirectional sync above is a separate feature. SSO-only accounts and additional authentication are not automated. Check connection errors for your organization's support limits.

Leave recognition

Enable the module and automatic-recognition option, then choose a source. It uses explicit morning-off and afternoon-off event titles only. It does not infer half-days from annual leave or a remaining balance. For shared calendars containing another person's leave, select today's mode manually or disable automatic recognition.

Plugin management · Calendar connections, conflicts and recovery · DaouOffice setup · Recognition limits

7. Choose a theme and icon

  1. Open Mac Settings → Appearance. Choose Soft mint, Warm stone, Blue gray, Dusty lavender or Charcoal.
  2. Adjust window background, sidebar, card, accent and text colors using the picker or a six-digit #RRGGBB value. Check the preview and contrast notice. Restore theme defaults when needed.
  3. Choose Original, Mint, Blue, Lavender or Graphite from the five built-in icons, or import a PNG/JPEG image.

Custom images support up to 20MB and 8192px per side. The in-app preview and running app icon change. The installed bundle and Finder icon stay unchanged, so an old icon in Finder is expected. The imported original file is preserved.

Appearance preferences are separate from attendance records. Windows 1.5.13 does not have this Appearance interface. Appearance details

8. View and preserve records

On Mac, open Settings → Arrival history, change the month and select a date. Check arrival, mode and automatic/manual source. Choose Open records folder to find the local data. This view does not fill in or edit past attendance.

Mac attendance lives in ~/Library/Application Support/AfterSix/state.json. Windows Settings → Recent history lists the 30 latest arrivals; General shows the local file location: %LOCALAPPDATA%\HappyLulu\state.json.

Mac and Windows records do not sync with each other. Replacing the app keeps records outside the app. If a record cannot be read, the app preserves the original and stops saving; do not reset or delete it. For a backup, quit the app and copy the local record file to a safe location.

Basic attendance is not collected remotely, and the app does not collect keyboard or screen activity. Optional calendar and DaouOffice connections communicate with their respective services. History views and storage

9. Update to a new version

Mac

Open Settings → Updates to check the app version and automatic-check/install preferences. By default the app checks at launch and hourly, then downloads and installs updates automatically. Existing saved preferences are respected.

Automatic restart waits until app windows are closed, the app is inactive, and arrival saving and calendar sync are idle. A prepared update can also install during normal quit. Once installation is prepared, settings changes are temporarily restricted until restart.

An old version with updates disabled, or an installation using the former site feed, may need one manual replacement with the latest Mac app. Quit and replace only the app in the same location. Do not delete attendance or connection files for an update.

Windows

Version 1.5.13 has no in-app automatic updater. Check the release list, download the new ZIP, quit, extract the full package and replace the app in its existing folder.

Update behavior and limits · Current Mac release · Windows release

10. Troubleshooting

No window appears. Where is the app?

HappyLulu lives in the menu bar or tray. Check the top of the Mac screen, or the Windows notification area and hidden icons. Open Settings from the Mac panel's settings button or the Windows tray right-click menu. After updating, launch the app in Applications or your fixed Windows folder rather than a copy in Downloads.

My arrival is missing.

Check that the app was running and observed an actual unlock, or a Mac login-item launch. Wake and manual launch alone do not create past attendance. Check the allowed window, observations before 06:00, and Day off today or annual / official leave. You can enter today's valid time manually.

The arrival time will not save.

Use today, no later than the current time, with 08:00–10:00 for regular work/afternoon off or 13:00–15:00 for morning off. A mode change is also rejected when the existing time is incompatible. Read the error and correct the input while keeping the original record.

Calendar access or events are missing.

Check Calendar installation and activation, feature routing, the account's calendar switch in macOS Internet Accounts and full calendar access. Click Allow calendar connection to request permission. Return after approving in System Settings, then choose the calendars to read. For DaouOffice errors, inspect Connection diagnostics; a person must answer a CAPTCHA. A failed fetch differs from an empty calendar.

My icon has not changed.

Check the running app and in-app preview. The Finder and installed bundle icons remain unchanged. An imported image must be PNG/JPEG, at most 20MB and 8192px per side.

A record or update error appears.

Keep the record file and note the displayed error and app version. Find its location in Settings without deleting it. Manually replace an old Mac app if automatic updates are unavailable. For Windows launch errors, check the x64 Desktop Runtime 10 and extraction of the full ZIP.

Review installation · Calendar setup steps · Find your records

11. Mac and Windows differences

  • Both: local arrival records, actual unlock detection, today's manual arrival, regular work and morning/afternoon off, work/break duration, last-Friday reduction, five time-display units, Korean/English and extra-time guidance.
  • Mac 1.5.18 build34: login-item detection, compact menu bar panel, four-digit autosave, five daily modes, monthly history, optional plugins, Calendar beta, DaouOffice reading, half-day recognition, themes/icons and automatic updates.
  • Windows 1.5.13: a tray today view, separate manual-entry/settings dialogs and a recent-history list. It does not include the new Mac panel, Lulu Day, annual / official leave, plugins, Calendar, Appearance settings or in-app automatic updates.

Mac requires macOS 13 or later and ships as Universal; Intel hardware testing is a separate remaining check. Windows requires Windows 10/11 x64. Attendance does not sync between devices or register in your company's official attendance system.
